images.filename: Awyrlun o Gastell y Bere yn Hydref 2024 - Aerial image of Welsh castle Castell y Bere near Tywyn, Gwynedd, Wales 50.png
images.caption:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.

Castell y Bere is a Welsh castle in south Gwynedd, Wales. It was one of the most important castles of the princes of Gwynedd in the 13th century. It was built by Llywelyn the Great to keep out the invading English. It is believed that the poet Gruffudd ab yr Ynad Goch composed his famous elegy for Prince Llywelyn ap Gruffudd (Llywelyn II) in Castell y Bere in December 1282 or early 1283.
images.alt:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.

images.filename: A view from the Pyg track towards Pen-y-pass - geograph.org.uk - 770076.jpg
images.caption: A view from the Pyg track towards Pen-y-pass In the foreground are some glaciated and crampon-worn rocks on the PYG track at the top of a steep staircase section.  Seen just above the rocks, and far below in the Llanberis Pass, is the white building of the Pen-y-pass YHA.  To the left is Llyn Cwmffynon with Glyder Fach above, and to the right the snowy domed mountain is Moel Siabod.

images.caption:
Llyn y Dywarchen above Rhyd Ddu in Snowdonia.
I found this one lurking in the files from last February. Another version is buried deep in my photostream but this shot has not seen the light of day before.
I remember this day very clearly, it was bitterly cold but the light was wonderful and not a breeze to be felt (this was taken without a tripod) or a sound to be heard and once again I had the lake completely to myself.
